question.text: A long solenoid with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn><mo> </mo><mi>turns</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> has a core material with relative permeability <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn></math> and volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>.</mo></math> If the core material is replaced by another material having relative permeability of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>750</mn></math> with same volume maintaining same current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>75</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> in the solenoid, the fractional change in the magnetic moment of the core would be approximately <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>499</mn></mfrac></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math> Find the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
